# A select its slot builds afresh takes a choice, on every target.
#
# The click renders the panel again, and on gtk4 the drop-down with it. Its
# choices are offered by an effect keyed on the labels and the drop-down,
# and GTK handed the new drop-down the old one's address, so the key did not
# move and the new one was offered nothing: the second choice found no
# choice to select. An effect whose key reads a node now mounts again
# wherever the node is built (remountOnBuild), and a write the view reads
# settles it, so the click's own handler offers the new drop-down its
# choices.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component page ui.node {
    var shown = true
    var kind = "Red"
    var count = 0

    ui.vbox {
        if shown {
            ui.vbox {
                ui.text(value="{count}")
                ui.select #pick(:value=kind) {
                    ui.choice(label="Red")
                    ui.choice(label="Green")
                    ui.choice(label="Blue")
                }
            }
        }
        ui.button #more(text="more", @click { count += 1 })
    }
}

ui.window {
    page()
}

func testAChoiceAfterTheSelectIsBuiltAgain(t test.Test, c page) {
    if c.pick != null {
        c.pick.change("Green")
    }
    t.assert(c.kind == "Green")
    c.more.click()
    if c.pick != null {
        c.pick.change("Blue")
    }
    t.assert(c.kind == "Blue")
}
